affectedCopies: No copies. GppPermit and GppPermitObservation are read only by the GPP verdict code; no projection, graph mirror or AI context reads them.
ToolExecution.gppPermitId / gppPermitVerdict duplicate the observation's verdict onto the existing audit row by design, so the authority trail shows it without a join.

Identifiers that are deliberately not foreign keys use *Ref/*Key column names (FK Index Coverage guard): a lineage reference must be able to go missing and be recorded as lineage_missing (PR-D), and audit evidence must outlive its referent.

privacyAssessment.sensitivity: internal: security-audit evidence keyed by internal user and agent ids already present on ToolExecution
privacyAssessment.dataSubjectRights: Holds no names, contact data, tool parameters or results. Follows ToolExecution's 365-day telemetry-bounded security-audit retention (the @dpf lifecycle tag enrolls both tables in the retention sweep).
privacyAssessment.reviewDisposition: Audit-only in PR-C: no verdict changes a call's outcome. Read by operators and the later promotion review (PR-E).

migration.name: 20261001180000_gpp_shadow_permits
migration.backfill: None. Creates three enums and two empty tables, and adds two nullable columns to ToolExecution. No existing row is read or rewritten; an older ToolExecution row reads NULL, meaning 'recorded before permits existed'. IF NOT EXISTS and duplicate_object guards make a re-run harmless, so it applies on any data state.
migration.rollback: Forward-only. Reverting the code leaves the tables and columns unused and harmless.
